display.title: Beis Adar: The Broken Esrog, a Story of Uncle Yossi's Mother
display.summary_short: On his mother's yahrzeit, Uncle Yossi tells how, as a girl of seven, she carried her father's esrog from house to house so everyone could do the mitzvah, and what happened when it broke.
display.summary_long: On Beis Adar, the yahrzeit of his mother, Uncle Yossi tells a story from her childhood. Her father, a man of modest means, always paid top price for the most beautiful esrog and lulav in town. On Hoshana Rabbah, the last day to shake them, the seven-year-old girl asked to take them from house to house so that neighbors without a set could make the brachah. Her father agreed, but warned her that if the pitum, the tip of the esrog, broke, it could no longer be used. After the last house, skipping happily, she tripped, and the pitum broke off. She sat crying until a kind tailor took the esrog into his shop and came back with it 'fixed with a long needle'. When she bravely told her father the whole story, he laughed with joy and did not scold her: she had meant well and shared a mitzvah with others. Uncle Yossi closes with a prayer for the elevation of his mother's soul.
display.lesson: Love mitzvos and share them with others; a child who means well and tells the truth deserves understanding, not scolding.
